newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower in mixed and dull trade as investors remain sidelined, waiting for political developments, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.43 percent, or 0.80 points, to 186.64 on very low turnover of 49 million shekels against 47 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.48 percent to 196.84.

"The only activity today was in the Maof shares and the volume was very low. We see a little bit of encouragement because of the peace talks between Israelis and Palestinians," said Jonathan Ross, vice-president at Nesuah Trading and Investment.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat met Israeli President Ezer Weizman in Caesarea on Tuesday. The meeting, Arafat's first public visit to Israel, is seen as another indication that Israel and the PLO had pulled back from the brink after the recent clashes that killed 74 people.
"It is a wait-and-see period. Two big things will affect the market in the near future: the talks with the Palestinians and the approval of the budget," Ross said.

The Finance Ministry said it will submit its 1997 budget to parliament at the end of the month without making any changes to the original proposal despite widespread criticism. Parliament has until the end of the year to approve the budget.
"The market is dead. Many shares were not traded at all. A total turnover of around 50 million shekels for the whole market is simply a joke," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.50 percent to 28,092 on volume of 4.7 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 2.25 percent to 140,289 on volume of 2.6 million shekels; and Super Sol, which closed unchanged at 7,300 on turnover of 2.6 million shekels.
